result.title: Embodied AI for Scientific Discovery: From Physical Action to Scientific Evidence
result.summary: Scientific experiments are increasingly selected, executed and interpreted by learned systems that act through physical interfaces. Robot learning builds physical competence, whereas AI for science chooses which experiment to run, each reporting different endpoints. This review treats their interface as one problem, embodied AI for science, where the experiment itself is partially observed: specimen state, apparatus state and measurement processes are latent, actions are costly and irreversible, and missingness depends on execution and outcome. We organize the literature by three closures operating at distinct levels: operational closure (the experiment realized is the one intended), epistemic closure (the result updates beliefs or selects subsequent experiments) and evidential closure (the record supports a claim). We analyze workflows through a record-linked evidence cycle - Record, Diagnose, Calibrate, Confirm - as analytic functions with feedback. A taxonomy crosses these closures with six delegated decisions and five embodiment classes. Our formulation separates commanded, realized and observed conditions and models diagnosis with explicit resource, risk and sample-change costs. We compare experiment-selection methods by terminal decision, review perception, protocol compilation, visuomotor policies, world models, recovery and transfer by evidence emission requirements, and compare chemistry, materials, biology, microscopy and field workflows by what their records establish. An appendix provides an evidence map of 28 workflows (26 physical, two software-boundary), characterizing validation pathways and claim confirmation requirements. We propose evaluation that separates actions, valid experiments, campaigns and confirmed claims, framing open challenges as controlled comparisons with measurable failure conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 这篇综述把机器人学习与 AI for science 统一为「embodied AI for science」，以操作闭环、认知闭环和证据闭环组织文献，并对实验选择、感知、世界模型和记录验证进行分类，提出区分动作、有效实验、研究活动与确证主张的评价框架。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对部分可观测的实验状态、昂贵且不可逆动作以及「记录—诊断—校准—确认」证据闭环的刻画，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、LOOK/STOP 决策与信念更新提供概念参照，但其与多模态推理的具体可迁移性仍需核查。
